chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn al-Ashʿath, from Dāwūd ibn Zurbī, who said:

I came to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام with some wealth, and he took part of it and left part of it. So I said, "May Allah set you right, for what reason did you leave it with me?" He said, "Indeed, the holder of this command will ask it of you." Then, when news of his death came to us, Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, his son, sent to me and asked me for that wealth, so I handed it over to him.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, the son who requested the remaining wealth
key_terms.أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, the Imam to whom the wealth was brought
key_terms.بِمَالٍ: with wealth; property or funds delivered to the Imam
key_terms.ذَلِكَ الْمَالَ: that specific wealth which had been left with the narrator
key_terms.صَاحِبَ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the holder of this affair; the rightful Imam and successor in authority

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the succession of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام after Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration relates an incident in which Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام intentionally left part of some wealth with the narrator and informed him that the next holder of the affair would request it. After the Imam's death, his son Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام asked for that wealth, and the narrator delivered it, reflecting continuity of the Imamate and recognition of the succeeding Imam.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Zahhak Bin Al Ash’as Bin Al Ash’ab, from Dawood Bin Zurby who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> with some wealth, so he<sup>asws</sup> took part of it and left part. So I said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! For which thing (reason) did you<sup>asws</sup> leave it to be with me?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Master of this command (Imamate), would seek it from you<sup>asws</sup>’. So when his<sup>asws</sup> Obituary came to us, Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> sent a message to me, asking me for that wealth. So I handed it over to him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from ad-Dahhak ibn al-Ash‘ath from Dawud ibn Zurbi who has said the following.

“Once I went to deliver some property to abu Ibrahim (a.s.). He accepted some of it and left the others. I asked him, “May Allah keep you well, why have you left it with me?” He said, “The in charge of this task (Leadership with Divine Authority) will demand it from you.” When we heard the news of his (abu Ibrahim’s) death, abu al-Hassan sent his son to me asking for that property and I delivered it to him.”
